The rows a fit was made from

Source: R/ilm_model.R, R/zzz-iml-aliases.R
ilm_data.Rd

The fit's model frame, with the variables its transformed terms are built from added back. The frame holds a transformed term as its own column, such as log(x) or poly(t, 2), and not the variable underneath it. So code that places new rows on a fit, to predict at changed values of x or t or to tell which rows lie beyond the data, cannot rebuild the term from the frame alone. From these rows, predict() and model.matrix() can.

Usage

ilm_data(object)

Arguments

object

A fitted "ilm_model" object.

Value

A data frame: the model frame, with the added columns after its own. NULL for a fit that has no model frame.

Details

The columns added are those of data that the model frame lacks and that the model names: in its formula, in a dispersion or zero-inflation formula, or, for a correlation over time given by its columns, as in ilm_ar1(~ t | g), its time and group. They are matched to the frame's rows by row name, so after rows are dropped for missing values they are the fit's own rows.

Nothing is added, and the frame is returned alone, when data was not a data frame, when its row names do not all match the frame's, or when the frame already holds every variable the model names, as when nothing in it is transformed. A fit made before these columns were kept also returns its frame alone.

See also

model.frame.ilm_model() for the frame alone.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(t = rep(1:12, 10), g = factor(rep(1:10, each = 12)))
d$y <- 0.2 * d$t + stats::rnorm(10)[d$g] + stats::rnorm(120)
f <- ilm_model(y ~ poly(t, 2) + (1 | g), data = d, family = "gaussian",
               verbose = FALSE)
names(model.frame(f))   # the frame holds poly(t, 2), not t
#> [1] "y"          "poly(t, 2)" "g"         
head(ilm_data(f))       # t is added back
#>            y poly(t, 2).1 poly(t, 2).2 g t
#> 1  1.0853274 -0.145443618  0.158691998 1 1
#> 2  0.1633894 -0.118999324  0.072132726 1 2
#> 3 -0.6476944 -0.092555030  0.002885309 1 3
#> 4 -2.0411537 -0.066110736 -0.049050254 1 4
#> 5  1.4984771 -0.039666441 -0.083673963 1 5
#> 6  0.5286126 -0.013222147 -0.100985817 1 6
